LanguageData.ARIOIAF_OldGodsNarrative: Before septs and crowns, the children of the forest listened to the gods of stream, stone, and wood. The First Men took up their worship, swearing their oaths before the carved faces of the weirwoods. These nameless gods demand neither scripture nor priesthood; their witnesses are the ancient trees, and their temples the quiet godswoods.\n\nAn oath must be kept, a guest beneath one’s roof protected, and the dead remembered. Winter teaches humility: stores must be gathered, kin sheltered, and hardship endured. Beneath the red leaves, the old gods watch in silence.
LanguageData.ARIOIAF_FaithOfTheSevenNarrative: There is one god with seven faces, each revealing a different truth of mortal life. The Father judges, the Mother grants mercy, and the Warrior lends courage. The Maiden guards innocence, the Smith honors labor, and the Crone lights the path of wisdom. The Stranger waits beyond every life, feared yet never absent.\n\nIn septs great and humble, the faithful light candles and seek guidance through prayer. Septons and septas teach justice tempered by compassion, duty upheld through honest service, and strength used to defend the weak. From a child’s first blessing to the final farewell, the Seven bear witness.
